subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call instead?
rationale: The issue touches a sandbox execution boundary and the report explicitly accepts either warning or error behavior, so automation should not choose the stricter product/security policy alone.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warning channel while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a different host or elevated path when they require an interactive terminal.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Fork PR
options.body: After choosing the behavior, adopt the open fork PR or replace it with a target-repo PR that includes docs and proof.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warning channel while preserving current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest history signal for both the original PTY behavior and the adjacent exec runtime/routing refactors.
